prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet: the DIVE ATTACK of the HARPY, a winged hag that hangs under a dungeon's ceiling and then dives at the player's head talons first, for a Doom/Hexen-style first-person game where monsters are drawn as sprites from several camera angles.

REFERENCE IMAGES, in the order attached:
1. The harpy's turnaround sheet (front, front three-quarter, side, rear three-quarter, back). It is the character design: a gaunt hag with grey leathery skin, a hooked, beak-like nose, a shrieking mouth of small yellowed teeth, glowing sickly yellow eyes and long matted ash-grey hair; a body of ragged slate and soot-brown feathers; ARMS THAT ARE WINGS, with three long, bony, rust-clawed fingers at each wing's bend; scaly dark bird legs with big hooked rust-coloured talons; a short fan of tail feathers. Also the shading style.
2. The harpy hovering, seen from THIS sheet's camera view. Match its camera angle, the way it faces, its pixel size, outline weight and scale exactly.

The harpy has exactly two wings and two legs in every frame, and no human arms or hands besides the clawed fingers at the wings' bends. The face, hair, eyes and talons look the same in every frame.

LAYOUT
- One horizontal row of 3 equal cells, read left to right: cell 1 the hovering copy, cell 2 the wind-up, cell 3 the dive. Make the cells wide enough for the wings at their widest, with the harpy drawn small enough to fit.
- Background: flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no gradient, texture, vignette, glow, cast shadow or floor.
- The cells are separated by thin vertical lines of pure cyan (#00FFFF), each running the full height of the image.
- Cell 1 is a plain copy of reference 2: the harpy hovering, wings raised in a high V, in exactly the same pose. It sets the scale for the other frames, which are drawn at the same scale: the body, head and legs are exactly as big in every cell.
- The whole figure, including both wingtips and the talons, fits inside each cell with a clear magenta margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or a cyan line, and nothing is cropped.
- No text, labels, numbers, frame borders, speed lines, motion blur, smear trails, loose feathers, dust or effects. Only the harpy.
- Crisp pixel art with hard edges and no anti-aliasing against the magenta. No semi-transparent pixels, and no pink or purple glow bleeding into the background.

THE POSES (the target is in front of the harpy, where it faces):
- Frame 2 (cell 2), WIND-UP, the warning before the dive: the harpy rears back in the air, the body leaning back, the wings spread wide and high, fully fanned, the head thrown back in a shriek, the legs drawn up and forward with the talons raised and wide open, ready to grab.
- Frame 3 (cell 3), DIVE: the harpy plunges forward and down at its target, the body tilted steeply forward along the dive, the head low and thrust forward, the hair streaming back, the wings swept back close along the body, half folded, and both legs thrust forward ahead of the head with the talons open and reaching for the target.

VIEW: back, as in the fifth cell of reference 1 and in reference 2. The harpy faces straight away from the viewer in every cell: we see its back, the tops of its wings, the back of its head with the matted hair, and the tail fan; the face doesn't show. In the dive it plunges straight away from the viewer.

REFERENCE IMAGE 3 is the finished animation seen from the FRONT, laid out the same way (cell 1 hovering, then the frames). It is the same animation this sheet must show: the same poses, the same wing positions, the same timing. Only the camera angle changes, to the one in reference 2.
